merger_name: ANZ Australian Staff Superannuation Scheme – further investment in Vinva Australian Equities Fund unit trust

anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services

merger_description:
The proposed acquisition is the issue of units in the Vinva Australian Equities Fund (the **Vinva Fund**) to ANZ Staff Superannuation (Australia) Pty Limited (the **Super Trustee**) in its capacity as trustee of the ANZ Australian Staff Superannuation Scheme (the **Scheme**), in consideration for the Super Trustee investing $150 million into the Vinva Fund as a passive investment (the **Acquisition**).

The Super Trustee is a non-controlled subsidiary of Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Limited (**ANZ**). ANZ and other ANZ subsidiaries (who are connected entities of the Super Trustee) provide banking and other financial services in Australia and internationally to wholesale and retail clients. ANZ also offers investment advisory services to individual investors under its ‘Private Bank’ brand, which includes giving advice about, and arranging investments in, managed investment products.

The sole business of the Super Trustee is the provision of superannuation benefits and superannuation products to current and former ANZ Bank group employees and their spouses/partners in the Super Trustee’s capacity as trustee of the Scheme, an APRA-regulated complying superannuation fund.  

Vinva Investment Management Limited (**Vinva**), the operator and responsible entity of the Vinva Fund, operates in the market of providing managed investment products to wholesale and, indirectly, retail investors throughout Australia.

The Acquisition would increase the Super Trustee’s existing holding in the Vinva Fund to more than 20% of the issued units. The Super Trustee’s involvement with the Vinva Fund and Vinva is as a passive investor in investments offered by the Vinva, including the Vinva Fund.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. the Acquisition does not result in any substantive change in
the control of the Vinva Fund, or the control of the entities
which the Vinva Fund has interests in
b. while the broader ANZ corporate group (through its ‘Private
Bank’ brand) and Vinva overlap in the supply of managed
investment products, the Super Trustee must perform its
duties and exercise its powers in the best financial interests
of the Scheme’s beneficiaries.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
